Transcript: Domestication syndrome. Select an animal for tameness and for nothing else, and along with the tameness you are supposed to get a suite of traits nobody bred for: piebald coats, floppy ears, shortened faces, curly tails, a juvenile playfulness that carries on into adult life. One lever, a whole package. The neural crest account supplied the machinery for it - a slight shortfall in the cells that migrate out early in development, the cells that go on to build pigment, cartilage and the adrenal glands, would reach every item on that list at once. The account rode in on the coat-tails of the Novosibirsk foxes. Its own predictions, about cell numbers and about migration timing, have so far been checked in one species.

Lord's objection is archival, and as far as the pelts go it is unanswerable. The founding animals came off a fur farm on Prince Edward Island and had been bred in captivity for some forty years before Belyaev took delivery of them, already carrying piebald patches, already handleable - though how handleable depends on what the farm's records were counting. Whatever the founders walked in with, the programme cannot book as earnings. The coats, certainly.

There are people who take the whole business as an artefact of the writing-up: the trait list was put together by going through domesticates and noting down what they had, so of course domesticates have it, and there was never any package there to be explained.

Novosibirsk ran a second line out of those same founders, in the same sheds, on the same feed, selected for the opposite response to an approaching hand. Between those two lines the cortisol curves separate, and so does the window in which a pup will walk up to something it has never seen before: in the tame line it stays open for weeks after it has shut in the other.

Horses have been handled since the Botai. Their ears stand up. Their faces are as long as a tarpan's. Pintos are everywhere, in every stockyard on earth.

Selection against the fear response moves the timing of a developmental window. Whichever tissues are still finishing their work inside that window may be carried along with it, or may be left exactly where they were, according to the species and to whatever else the breeder had an eye on at the time.
prompt: [Academic Talk - Evolutionary Biology] Given the evidence the lecturer sets out, what remains of the original claim about tameness and the trait list?
choices: That the cells migrating out early in development supply pigment, cartilage and the adrenal glands, so any shortfall in them must express itself across every structure those cells reach.
That the traits gathered under the name were only ever the traits somebody thought to write down, so that nothing is left standing that calls for an explanation at all.

That breeding against fear shifts when a developmental window opens and shuts, and the other traits come along only where they happen to be under construction at that moment - so the list names what one change can permit rather than what it delivers.
That the full package appears only where the founding stock is genuinely wild, a condition the Prince Edward Island animals failed to meet.
correct_answer: That breeding against fear shifts when a developmental window opens and shuts, and the other traits come along only where they happen to be under construction at that moment - so the list names what one change can permit rather than what it delivers.
explanation: C2 rather than C1 because nothing in the talk announces which version survives: the speaker never says what is left, never grades the positions, and states the narrowed claim as a flat mechanical remark in the last paragraph with no marker that it is the conclusion. The listener has to work out that the two-line comparison rescues something the founder-stock objection cannot touch, that the horse case breaks the co-occurrence rather than the effect, and that the only version both results permit is a timing claim with contingent followers - while three fluent alternatives are each supported by one paragraph read in isolation.

prompt: [Academic Talk - Evolutionary Biology] Take the proposition that the divergence in the fear window between the two Novosibirsk lines is a genuine product of the selection programme. Who in the talk is committed to it?
choices: Lord is, and the lecturer follows him in it; it is the ground the two of them share against the original claim.
The lecturer is, and Lord is not: Lord's objection reaches the animals the programme began with, whereas this comparison is drawn between two lines bred out of those same animals.
Lord and the readers who treat the trait list as an artefact of the writing-up are both committed to it, while the lecturer holds back from it.
Nobody in the talk is committed to it; it belongs to the original claim that the later evidence is brought in to complicate.
correct_answer: The lecturer is, and Lord is not: Lord's objection reaches the animals the programme began with, whereas this comparison is drawn between two lines bred out of those same animals.
explanation: C2 rather than C1 because the three parties are separated only by how they are handled, never by a stated verdict: Lord's objection is twice fenced in ('as far as the pelts go', 'the coats, certainly'), the artefact reading is reported once and left without support or comment, and the lecturer's own commitment is visible only as the unqualified claim the evidence paragraphs happen to build toward. A listener who registers that the lecturer agreed with Lord somewhere - and he did, about the coats - will carry that concession across to a result Lord's argument structurally cannot reach, which is exactly the conflation option A rewards.

prompt: [Academic Talk - Evolutionary Biology] The lecturer turns to horses for three sentences and moves on without comment. What work is the example doing?
choices: It shows that horses were bred for work and for biddability rather than for tameness in the relevant sense, so the conditions for the syndrome were never in place.
It dates the appearance of the trait list against the archaeological record, the Botai giving the earliest secure point of comparison.
It establishes coat pattern as the one item dependable enough to identify a domesticated population from bones and hides.
It shows the items on the list coming apart - one of them present and conspicuous, the others absent - under precisely the long selection that was supposed to deliver them together.
correct_answer: It shows the items on the list coming apart - one of them present and conspicuous, the others absent - under precisely the long selection that was supposed to deliver them together.
explanation: C2 rather than C1 because the horse paragraph is four bare declaratives with no connective to the argument on either side of it, so its function has to be reconstructed from what it would damage and what it would leave intact. Getting it requires seeing that the pintos are as load-bearing as the upright ears - the example works by pairing a hit with two misses, dissociating the list rather than denying that selection does anything - and a listener who reads the paragraph as a counterexample to domestication effects in general takes A.

That it acquired its standing from the celebrity of the fox programme rather than from any testing of what it predicts on its own.
That it was formulated only once the fox programme was well under way, and could therefore be shaped around results that were already in.
That it has been carried along by researchers who apply the fox programme's breeding regime to one species after another.
correct_answer: That it acquired its standing from the celebrity of the fox programme rather than from any testing of what it predicts on its own.
explanation: C2 rather than C1 because the idiom's parts are both live in this talk - coats and tails are two of the five traits named a few lines earlier - so the compositional reading is not merely available but pre-loaded, and it points straight at option A. Settling it means carrying the phrase forward into the very next sentence, where the account's own predictions are said to have been checked in a single species, and inferring that the sentence is there to say what the account's standing did not come from; nothing in the talk glosses the idiom or contrasts it with anything.
